featured.title: The US Has Run Out of EB-2 Green Cards for Indians This Year. No More Approvals Until October.
featured.excerpt: The State Department confirmed that all EB-2 immigrant visa numbers for India-born applicants have been exhausted for FY2026, freezing final residency approvals for thousands of skilled professionals.
featured.nri_angle: The EB-2 freeze directly affects hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals in the US on H-1B visas waiting for permanent residency.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: New York's Indian-Origin Mayor Just Launched His Own DOGE. Jeff Bezos Agreed With Him.
news.excerpt: Zohran Mamdani's Commission on Government Efficiency is designed to do what Elon Musk's version never could: make government work without burning it down.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Supreme Court Just Set a 3-Month Deadline for High Courts to Deliver Judgments. India Has 5.49 Crore Cases Pending.
news.excerpt: Bail orders must now be delivered the same day. If a reserved judgment is not pronounced in 90 days, the case can be reassigned to another bench.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Replaced Its Top Military Commander and Navy Chief on the Same Day. Here Is What Changes.
news.excerpt: General Anil Chauhan retired after four decades in uniform. His successor inherits an unfinished revolution in how India fights wars.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Committed to Buying $500 Billion in American Goods. Economists Say the Math Does Not Add Up.
news.excerpt: After Secretary of State Marco Rubio's India visit, trade experts and economists are questioning whether a $100-billion-a-year import target is feasible — or wise — for an economy already strained by a weak rupee and rising oil prices.
news.nri_angle: A stronger US-India economic relationship supports the policy environment sustaining H-1B visas and bilateral business ties. But if the $500B commitment is perceived as one-sided, it risks fuelling political backlash that has already led to tariff escalations and immigration crackdowns affecting NRIs.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An Indian American Teenager Just Won the National Spelling Bee. He Set a Record Doing It.
news.excerpt: Shrey Parikh, 14, from Rancho Cucamonga, California, spelled 32 words in 90 seconds to shatter the Scripps National Spelling Bee spell-off record. The winning word was bromocriptine.
news.nri_angle: Parikh continues the Indian American Spelling Bee dynasty — 28 of the last 34 champions have been Indian American. The pattern reflects H-1B-era immigration, high-income Indian American households, and a network of South Asian spelling circuits that have transformed the competition.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Pentagon Just Called India a 'Critical Anchor' in the Indo-Pacific. Then It Announced Javelin Co-Production.
news.excerpt: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth used his Shangri-La Dialogue keynote to praise India's military modernisation, announce Javelin missile co-production, and demand that all Asian allies spend 3.5 percent of GDP on defence.
news.nri_angle: A deepening US-India defence partnership — now including Javelin co-production — reinforces the geopolitical alignment that underpins H-1B policy, trade deals, and bilateral business ties. Defence-corridor manufacturing jobs in India could create new career pathways for dual-citizen professionals.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The UK Foreign Secretary Is Visiting India Next Week. The Free Trade Deal They Signed Is Already in Trouble.
news.excerpt: Yvette Cooper will meet S. Jaishankar to discuss the Russia-Ukraine war, Ebola, and trade. But London's new steel tariffs have created the first major friction point in an agreement that was supposed to be the UK's biggest post-Brexit prize.
news.nri_angle: 1.9 million people of Indian heritage in the UK form the 'living bridge.' The trade deal promised easier business travel and reduced costs. UK steel tariffs threaten that promise and small business owners who import Indian goods face higher costs.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Power Grid Just Hit 270 Gigawatts of Peak Demand. Coal India Is Scrambling to Keep Up.
news.excerpt: A record-breaking heatwave has pushed India's electricity consumption to an all-time high. Twenty-one power plants have critically low coal stocks. Blackouts are spreading from Gurugram to Bihar.
news.nri_angle: NRIs with family in India are hearing reports of load-shedding, water tanker shortages, and elderly relatives suffering without AC. The 270 GW demand peak and coal supply scramble expose the gap between India's tech-power ambitions and its grid infrastructure reality.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: AUKUS Just Signed Its First Undersea Drone Pact. India Is Not Part of It.
news.excerpt: The US, UK, and Australia will jointly develop unmanned underwater vehicles to protect seabed cables and project power. Deliveries begin in 2027. India — a Quad partner but not an AUKUS member — faces hard questions about its own undersea ambitions.
news.nri_angle: Indian-origin defence technology professionals work across the US, UK, and Australian defence sectors. India's exclusion from AUKUS undersea tech raises questions about NRI-connected defence innovation pipelines and India's strategic tier in the Indo-Pacific.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The US and Iran Have Reached a Ceasefire Extension Deal on Paper. Neither Leader Has Signed It.
news.excerpt: The 60-day memorandum would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, lift the US naval blockade, and begin nuclear talks. Trump says he is in no rush. Iran says its Hormuz controls are permanent. India is watching its oil lifeline.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India and Canada Just Launched a Trade Forum and Set a Deadline to Finish Their Free Trade Deal. The Thaw Is Real.
news.excerpt: Commerce Minister Goyal led the largest Indian delegation ever sent abroad. Canada will send a trade mission to India later this year. Defence cooperation talks followed.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.excerpt: The State Department confirmed that all EB-2 immigrant visa numbers for India-born applicants have been exhausted for FY2026, freezing final residency approvals for thousands of skilled professionals.
news.nri_angle: The EB-2 freeze directly affects hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals in the US on H-1B visas waiting for permanent residency.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The US Economy Grew Just 1.6 Percent Last Quarter. That Is Worse Than Anyone Expected.
news.excerpt: A sharp downward revision to first-quarter GDP, driven by weaker consumer spending and the Iran war's inflationary toll, signals trouble ahead for hiring, mortgages, and the Indian professionals who depend on both.
news.nri_angle: A slowing US economy directly impacts the 4.8 million Indian-origin Americans through hiring freezes, H-1B sponsorship pullbacks, higher mortgage rates, reduced remittance purchasing power, and a political environment less receptive to immigration reform. India received $129B in remittances in FY2025 — any US economic slowdown ripples directly to families back home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Seventy Percent of Karachi Has No Reliable Water. India's Indus Treaty Suspension Is Only Part of the Story.
news.excerpt: Pakistan's financial capital faces a severe water crisis as the Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance. But the real causes run deeper than geopolitics.
news.nri_angle: The Indus Waters Treaty was a cornerstone of India-Pakistan relations that the diaspora followed closely. Its suspension signals a new phase in India's strategic posture, while the Karachi crisis exposes how infrastructure failures — not just geopolitics — drive water scarcity in the subcontinent.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Quad Just Agreed to Build a Port in Fiji and Launch a Critical Minerals Pact. India Hosted It All.
news.excerpt: The 11th Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi produced the grouping's first joint infrastructure project, a framework for critical minerals supply chains, and a maritime surveillance system — signalling the alliance is moving past photo-ops into operational territory.
news.nri_angle: The Quad Critical Minerals Initiative Framework directly benefits Indian tech and manufacturing supply chains. For NRIs in tech and defence industries, alternative supply chains away from China reduce geopolitical risk. The energy security initiative addresses the Hormuz disruption that has raised fuel costs affecting remittance value and Indian market returns.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Supreme Court Just Called the NEET Paper Leak 'Very Traumatic.' The Government Said Modi Is Personally Supervising.
news.excerpt: Justices Narasimha and Aradhe told the NTA to learn from the UPSC, the CBI is probing a Maharashtra conspiracy ring, and a retest is set for June 21 — the second NEET cancellation in three years.
news.nri_angle: For Indian families abroad who send their children to take NEET for medical college admissions in India, the disruption is acutely painful. Many candidates travel to India specifically for the exam, arranging accommodation, coaching, and leave. A cancellation followed by a retest weeks later imposes enormous logistical and emotional costs.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The UAE Secretly Struck Iran Dozens of Times During the War. 3.5 Million Indians Live There.
news.excerpt: A Wall Street Journal investigation reveals the Emirates carried out coordinated strikes on Iranian targets from the war's earliest days through the ceasefire — a far deeper military role than Gulf nations publicly acknowledged, with direct implications for the region's largest expatriate community.
news.nri_angle: An estimated 3.5 million Indians live and work in the UAE — the largest Indian expatriate community in any single country. The revelation that the UAE was an active combatant, not a neutral bystander, directly affects the security calculus for Indian professionals and families who remained in the country throughout the conflict.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The India-US Trade Deal Is Down to the Last 1 Percent. A Delegation Arrives in Delhi Next Week.
news.excerpt: Ambassador Sergio Gor says the deal could be signed within weeks. But the 'last 1 percent' is the hardest part — and the legal landscape under it has shifted.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: June 15 Is Two Weeks Away. Most Indian Americans With Accounts Back Home Still Haven't Filed What the IRS Wants.
nri-world.excerpt: The extended tax deadline for Americans abroad is approaching, and for the millions of Indian Americans holding dormant EPF, PPF, and NPS accounts in India, the FBAR and FATCA reporting obligations remain a minefield of overlapping forms, rising penalties, and genuinely unsettled law.
nri-world.nri_angle: Nearly every Indian American who worked in India before emigrating holds at least one dormant account — an EPF balance from a first job, a PPF account opened by a parent, an NPS contribution that stopped the day they flew out. These balances compound quietly in rupees while US reporting obligations compound loudly in dollars.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Australia Just Halved Its Regional Migration Intake. Indian Professionals Are Wondering What Happened to the Welcome Mat.
nri-world.excerpt: Regional skilled visas slashed from 33,000 to 14,110 for 2026-27, the 491 pathway trimmed by 23 per cent, and a new IDP report says a quarter of Indian students now call visa uncertainty their biggest barrier to studying abroad.
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian professionals in healthcare, engineering, and hospitality — the backbone of regional Australia's migrant workforce — face the sharpest impact. The cuts rewrite the calculus for tens of thousands of Indians who planned their careers around the regional pathway.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Canada's Duty-Free Shops Just Got an 'Indian Aisle.' It Matters More Than You Think.
nri-world.excerpt: Indian beverages have landed in airport duty-free stores across Toronto, Vancouver, and Alberta — the first time Indian brands have occupied premium retail space in Canada's travel corridor.
nri-world.nri_angle: For decades, Indians abroad have carried products from home in suitcases. Now Indian brands are arriving through the front door of international retail — and the 1.9 million-strong Canadian Indian diaspora helped make it possible.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's Commerce Minister Just Toured Canada for Three Days. The Diaspora Was the Subtext of Every Meeting.
nri-world.excerpt: Piyush Goyal's visit to Toronto and Ottawa was officially about CEPA negotiations and clean energy. Unofficially, it was a demonstration of how 1.9 million Indo-Canadians have become India's most effective trade envoys.
nri-world.nri_angle: India's trade diplomacy increasingly treats its diaspora not as a sentimental connection but as economic infrastructure. Goyal's Canada trip made that explicit.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Your Ancestral Home in Punjab Was Just Sold. You Weren't There. You Didn't Know. A Court Says This Is Now a Pattern.
nri-world.excerpt: A Punjab and Haryana High Court ruling lays bare the growing epidemic of property fraud targeting NRIs — and explains why most victims never get their land back.
nri-world.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs own property in India they rarely visit. This court case exposes how their absence is being systematically exploited — and what they can do before it happens to them.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Three Months Into the Iran War, Four Million Gulf NRIs Are Still Waiting for Normal. It Isn't Coming Soon.
nri-world.excerpt: Cancelled flights, shuttered schools, disrupted remittances, and a Strait of Hormuz that may not fully reopen until a peace deal sticks — the war's collateral damage to the Gulf's Indian community keeps compounding.
nri-world.nri_angle: The Gulf is home to roughly four million Indians — the largest single concentration of NRIs anywhere in the world. They drive taxis in Dubai, run trading firms in Sharjah, teach in CBSE schools in Kuwait, and wire billions in remittances home every year. Three months into the Iran war, every layer of that life has been disrupted. Flights home are cancelled or rerouted. Board exams were scrapped. Remittance corridors are squeezed. And the ceasefire that was supposed to bring normalcy keeps slipping. For a diaspora community that has spent decades building stability in a volatile region, this is the worst sustained disruption since the 1990 Gulf War evacuations.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Indian Diaspora Wants a Museum in Washington. Eight Years Later, They're Finally Ready to Build It.
nri-world.excerpt: A 501(c)(3) led by Atlanta-based educationist Dr Amitabh Sharma is preparing to raise $12-14 million for a 20,000-square-foot India Heritage Center in the US capital — the first museum in America dedicated entirely to India's 11,000-year civilisational story.
nri-world.nri_angle: The proposed India Heritage Center speaks to a gap that millions of Indian Americans have felt for decades: the absence of a permanent, authoritative institution in the United States that tells India's story on India's terms. For a diaspora that has built temples, endowed university chairs, and funded political campaigns, the lack of a dedicated museum in a city lined with them has been a quiet embarrassment. This project would give second- and third-generation Indian Americans a place to encounter their civilisational inheritance — and give non-Indian Americans a reason to understand the culture behind the fastest-growing immigrant community in the country.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: An Essay Competition Is Quietly Teaching Indian American Kids to Care About India. It's Working.
nri-world.excerpt: The India Philanthropy Alliance's Youth Essay Competition is in its seventh year. Past winners have directed grants to Indian nonprofits, joined leadership councils, and landed at UC Berkeley. The real product is dinner-table conversations between generations.
nri-world.nri_angle: The competition addresses a core diaspora challenge: how do you sustain philanthropic engagement with India across generations when the second generation's connection to the country is mediated through family stories rather than direct experience?
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Indian Restaurant Congress Just Went International. London Was the Obvious First Stop.
nri-world.excerpt: India Week 2026 hosted the industry's first global summit at the Royal Lancaster London. With 12,000 Indian restaurants and £4–5 billion in annual revenue, the UK market has outgrown the curry house era.
nri-world.nri_angle: The UK's Indian restaurant industry is a diaspora creation — built by immigrants, scaled by their children, and now being institutionalised through global platforms that connect operators from London to Dubai to Singapore.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: An Indian American Firm Just Bid $300 Million for FIFA World Cup India Rights. The Bigger Story Is Why India Still Doesn't Have a Broadcaster.
nri-world.excerpt: With the tournament two weeks away and no Indian deal in sight, a Washington DC-based investment firm is making an audacious play — while the Delhi High Court asks why 1.4 billion fans might face a total blackout.
nri-world.nri_angle: An Indian American investment firm from Washington DC is stepping into a gap that Indian domestic broadcasters have left open — a pattern increasingly visible across diaspora entrepreneurship, from media rights to restaurant franchises to technology ventures.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: America's Highest Astronautics Honour Just Went to Chandrayaan-3. India's Ambassador Accepted It in Washington.
nri-world.excerpt: The AIAA's Goddard Astronautics Award — named for the father of rocketry — was presented to ISRO's lunar mission at the ASCEND 2026 Conference, with Ambassador Vinay Kwatra using the moment to pitch deeper US-India space collaboration.
nri-world.nri_angle: The award ceremony in Washington, with India's Ambassador accepting on ISRO's behalf, crystallises a moment the diaspora has been building toward: Indian scientific achievement recognised at the highest level of American aerospace, in a city where Indian-origin engineers and scientists have been part of the space establishment for decades.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Wonder Just Launched an Indian Food Brand Across 100 Locations. It Might Be the Moment Indian Cuisine Stops Being 'Ethnic' in America.
nri-world.excerpt: The fast-growing food hall company is testing Dabba in Philadelphia before a national rollout, while Michelin-starred Indienne heads to Hudson Yards and the US now has over 12,600 Indian restaurants. Something has shifted.
nri-world.nri_angle: The mainstreaming of Indian food in America is both a cultural milestone and an economic one for the diaspora — every tikka masala on a fast-casual menu normalises a cuisine that was once ghettoised as 'ethnic,' while Indian-origin restaurateurs lead much of the fine-dining revolution.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The RBI Decides on Rates This Week. So Does the US Jobs Report. NRI Investors Are Caught Between Two Central Banks With Very Different Problems.
markets-finance.excerpt: India's Monetary Policy Committee meets June 3-5 with analysts split between a hold and a hike, while US nonfarm payrolls on Friday could cement the case for the Fed's first rate increase. Here is what NRI investors should watch across both economies.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Kevin Warsh Just Finished His First Week as Fed Chair. Markets Are Already Betting He Will Be Forced to Raise Rates.
markets-finance.excerpt: Warsh was sworn in promising lower rates. But inflation at 3.8 per cent, oil prices 30 per cent above pre-war levels, and a nine-week stock rally have left him with almost no room to deliver. NRI investors face a June of dual central bank risk.
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with both dollar and rupee holdings face a uniquely dangerous June. The RBI decides on June 5 and the Fed on June 16-17. A hawkish Fed with a steady RBI would widen the rate differential, pressure the rupee, and accelerate capital outflows from Indian equities. India's MSCI EM weight has already halved to 11 per cent.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The US and Iran Have a Deal to Reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Markets Rallied. But a Reuters Analysis Says It May Change Nothing.
markets-finance.excerpt: A 60-day truce extension would lift shipping restrictions and require Iran to de-mine the strait within 30 days. But global oil reserves are running out, the PCE just hit 3.8 per cent, and Friday's US jobs report could push the Fed toward a rate hike. Here is what NRI investors should watch.
markets-finance.nri_angle: India imports 85 per cent of its crude oil. Every $10 rise in Brent costs India roughly $15 billion annually. The Hormuz deal directly affects the rupee, RBI rate decisions, NRI deposit rates, and inflation-sensitive portfolios held by diaspora investors.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Oil Analysts Have Raised Their 2026 Forecasts for the Third Time. The Era of $60 Brent May Be Over.
markets-finance.excerpt: Brent is now forecast to average $90.44 a barrel this year, up 40 per cent from February estimates. Middle East crude exports have halved. Even a ceasefire will not undo the structural damage quickly. Here is what NRI investors should understand.
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs with India exposure through mutual funds, NRE/NRO deposits, or direct equity holdings, elevated oil prices are the single biggest macro variable. A weaker rupee erodes dollar-denominated returns on Indian assets, remittances buy less due to fuel-driven domestic inflation, and rate-sensitive sectors face headwinds if the RBI is forced to hike.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: US Inflation Just Hit 3.8 Per Cent. Markets Are Now Pricing a Fed Rate Hike Over a Cut. Here Is What That Means for NRI Investors.
markets-finance.excerpt: The April PCE reading is the highest since May 2023. The S&P 500 has risen for nine straight weeks anyway. On June 5, both the US jobs report and the RBI rate decision land on the same day. Your portfolio in both countries is on the line.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Just Raised Gold Import Duty to 15 Per Cent. Demand Has Collapsed, Discounts Hit $106 an Ounce, and Jewellers Are Refusing to Stock Up.
markets-finance.excerpt: The duty hike from 6 to 15 per cent — the steepest in a decade — has frozen India's gold market. Retail footfall has cratered, dealers are quoting record discounts, and NRIs planning weddings or gifts face a significant cost increase.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The US Just Dropped Fraud Charges Against Gautam Adani. His Stock Surged 22 Per Cent in May. Here Is What NRI Investors Should Understand About What Happened.
markets-finance.excerpt: The DOJ criminal case is closed, the SEC has settled, and the Treasury resolved an Iran sanctions case for $275 million. Bernstein says the worst is over. But the Adani saga reshaped how global capital views Indian conglomerates — and that lesson has not been unlearned.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The Rupee Just Had Its Best Day in Two Months. Oil Dropped, the RBI Stepped In, and a US-Iran Truce Extension Is on the Table. Here Is What the Week Ahead Looks Like.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Indian currency surged 0.7 per cent to 95 per dollar on Friday after central bank intervention and a drop in crude prices. With the RBI meeting on June 5 and US jobs data on June 6, the next seven days will set the tone for Indian markets through the monsoon.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Indian Markets Just Closed Their Worst May in Three Years. The Nifty Lost 1.9 Per Cent, Foreign Investors Pulled $24 Billion, and the Monsoon Forecast Just Got Worse.
markets-finance.excerpt: A monthly scorecard for NRI investors: what went wrong, what went right, and what to watch in June as the RBI prepares to decide on rates amid a weakening monsoon and an unresolved oil crisis.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Forex Reserves Just Fell to a One-Year Low of $681 Billion. The RBI Is Burning Through Dollars to Defend the Rupee. Here Is What NRI Investors Should Watch.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India's war chest shrank by $7.5 billion in a single week. Ceasefire hopes briefly pushed the rupee past 95. But the rate hike question looming over June 5 will determine what comes next for your deposits, remittances, and home loans.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index Just Fell From 20 Per Cent to 11. If You Own an EM Index Fund, a Chunk of Your India Exposure Just Disappeared.
markets-finance.excerpt: The largest single-year weight reduction in MSCI's history for India could trigger billions in mechanical selling. Here is what NRI investors holding passive EM funds need to understand.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index has been cut from 20 per cent to 11.2 per cent.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: MSCI Just Added Paytm and Fortis Healthcare to Its Global Index. The Rebalancing Takes Effect Tomorrow and Could Push $2 Billion Into Indian Stocks.
markets-finance.excerpt: India's weight in the MSCI Global Standard index has risen to 19 per cent, its highest ever. For NRI investors watching $24 billion in foreign outflows this year, the passive money flowing back in tells a different story.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Nousheen Naz Has Now Scored in Every Game. India's U18 Women Beat Korea 3-1 to Top Their Asia Cup Pool.
sports.excerpt: The fifteen-year-old from Seoni converted a penalty stroke in the fourth minute, Shruti Kumari and Kiran Ekka added field goals, and India sit first in Pool A in Japan.
sports.nri_angle: India's junior hockey pipeline continues to produce talent at a pace that resonates with NRIs who grew up watching the sport. The U18 Asia Cup in Japan is streamed live, with early-morning starts for US East Coast viewers.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: She Practised With Bamboo Poles and Husk Sacks. Now Pooja Singh Is the Highest-Jumping Woman in Indian History.
sports.excerpt: The nineteen-year-old from a mason's family in rural Haryana cleared 1.93 metres to break a fourteen-year-old national record and win gold at the Asian U20 Championships in Hong Kong.
sports.nri_angle: India's all-time women's high jump record holder is a nineteen-year-old from a mason's family who trained with bamboo poles. Her CWG qualification and national record resonate with NRIs who follow Indian athletics and grassroots sport development stories.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Gauff Is Out. Rybakina Is Out. Sinner and Djokovic Are Gone. The 2026 French Open Has Lost Its Way.
sports.excerpt: The defending women's champion fell to Anastasia Potapova on Saturday. Across both draws, only Sabalenka and Swiatek still stand as past Grand Slam champions at Roland Garros.
sports.nri_angle: NRIs who follow tennis can catch the wide-open second week on Sony Sports Network and SonyLIV from India, with late-afternoon IST matchups aligning well with morning viewing on the US West Coast — a rare scheduling sweet spot for diaspora families.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Zee Will Broadcast the FIFA World Cup in India. Twelve Days Before Kickoff, Indian Fans Finally Have an Answer.
sports.excerpt: After weeks of uncertainty, Zee Entertainment is set to announce a broadcast deal with FIFA. Matches will air on Unite8 Sports channels and stream on Zee5 — ending fears of a World Cup blackout in one of football's biggest markets.
sports.nri_angle: NRIs in the US will watch the World Cup live at local venues across 16 American cities. For fans back home in India, weeks of uncertainty about whether the tournament would even be broadcast have finally ended with Zee's deal. The 2022 Qatar World Cup generated record late-night viewership in India. Indian-American firm Avni LLC also emerged as an unlikely broadcast contender. The time-zone disadvantage for IST audiences makes streaming on Zee5 essential for diaspora fans in India-friendly time zones.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Gukesh Has Won His First Classical Game at Norway Chess. Divya Deshmukh Has Taken the Lead in the Women's Tournament.
sports.excerpt: The world champion beat Praggnanandhaa in Round 5 after four frustrating rounds. Wesley So stunned Carlsen. And Divya Deshmukh overtook Bibisara Assaubayeva to lead the women's event in Oslo.
sports.nri_angle: Three Indian players — Gukesh, Pragg, and Divya Deshmukh — are competing at the highest level of classical chess simultaneously at Norway Chess 2026. Gukesh, 20, is the youngest world champion in history. Pragg sits second in the standings. Divya, 19, has taken the lead in the women's event. For NRI chess fans, this depth of Indian talent at the elite level is unprecedented.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Gabriel's Penalty Sailed Over the Bar. PSG Have Won Back-to-Back Champions League Titles.
sports.excerpt: Arsenal took the lead inside six minutes in Budapest but couldn't hold it. The first club to retain the Champions League since Real Madrid has done it from Paris.
sports.nri_angle: For millions of NRI football fans following the Premier League and European football, Arsenal's penalty heartbreak in Budapest and PSG's dynasty-forging back-to-back titles happened at prime-time IST. With the FIFA World Cup starting in America in twelve days, the stakes are personal for diaspora fans who will watch many of these players at venues across the US.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Pragg Against Gukesh in Oslo. India's Two Finest Chess Players Meet at Norway Chess Round 5.
sports.excerpt: Praggnanandhaa is second. Gukesh is last. Firouzja leads by two and a half points. The world champion needs a result against his compatriot.
sports.nri_angle: Two Indians at the world's strongest chess tournament — Pragg in second place, world champion Gukesh in last — face each other in Round 5. India now has two elite players in the world's top ten, a generational shift that NRI chess fans are watching with pride. Pragg's sister Vaishali won the Women's Candidates earlier this year. The Rameshbabu family's remarkable year is reshaping how the world sees Indian chess.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Have Not Beaten Bangladesh in Two Years. They Play Them in Goa Tomorrow With the Group on the Line.
sports.excerpt: Bangladesh have scored six and conceded one in their last two matches against India's women. Sunday's SAFF Championship group match in Margao could decide who tops the group.
sports.nri_angle: India's women's football team plays in front of home crowds at the SAFF Championship in Goa — one of the few opportunities for NRI fans to follow the team in a competitive home tournament. India have not won the SAFF Women's Championship in six years, and the Bangladesh match is the first genuine test of their campaign. The match streams on FanCode at 7:30 PM IST.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Unity Cup in London Ended Without a Single Goal. They Lost 1-0 to Zimbabwe in the Third-Place Match.
sports.excerpt: The Blue Tigers went to England for the first time in twenty-four years. They came back with two defeats, zero goals, and hard questions twelve days before the FIFA World Cup kicks off in America.
sports.nri_angle: The FIFA World Cup starts in America in twelve days, across cities with massive Indian diaspora populations. Indian football's absence from the tournament, combined with this goalless showing against lower-ranked opposition in London, sharpens the contrast for NRIs who will be surrounded by World Cup fever.

lifestyle-health.title: A Drug That Blocks Cortisol Just Cut the Risk of Death From Ovarian Cancer by 35 Per Cent. No Biomarker Testing Was Required.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Phase 3 ROSELLA trial found that adding the cortisol-blocking drug relacorilant to chemotherapy extended survival in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer patients — regardless of prior treatment history. The results, presented at ASCO 2026, could establish a new standard of care.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Head-to-Head Trial Found That One Prostate Cancer Drug Causes Half the Cognitive Decline of Another. Every Patient Who Switched Was on the Worse Drug.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The ARACOG trial, presented at ASCO 2026, is the first rigorous comparison of how two standard prostate cancer drugs affect memory, attention, and executive function. The results may change how doctors and families approach treatment decisions.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study of 139 Cancer Patients Found That Getting Immunotherapy in the Morning Cut Recurrence by 77 Per Cent. The Only Change Was the Clock.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Multiple ASCO 2026 presentations and a randomised trial in Nature Medicine now confirm that circadian timing of cancer treatment is not a footnote — it may be one of the most powerful free interventions in oncology.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated risks for several cancers including breast, oral, and stomach. Nearly five million Indian Americans navigate a healthcare system where treatment timing is assigned by clinic convenience, not biology. This zero-cost intervention — simply requesting a morning infusion slot — could meaningfully improve outcomes.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Mounjaro Outperformed Every Other GLP-1 Drug in a Two-Year Trial of Early Type 2 Diabetes Patients. 60 Per Cent Achieved Normal Blood Sugar.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The SURPASS-EARLY trial found that tirzepatide helped recently diagnosed patients reach glycaemic targets 4 to 12 weeks faster than semaglutide and produced sustained normal HbA1c levels in more than double the patients on competing drugs.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians have among the highest type 2 diabetes rates globally — 23 per cent prevalence among Indian Americans vs 11 per cent in the general US population. They develop diabetes a decade earlier and at lower BMI thresholds, making early aggressive treatment even more critical. The SURPASS-EARLY data directly supports earlier intervention with tirzepatide for this population.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Two Studies Just Proved That Long COVID Neurological Symptoms Are Caused by the Body Attacking Itself. Existing Drugs May Already Work.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Autoantibodies from long COVID patients caused fatigue, pain, and nerve damage when transferred to healthy mice — even two years after infection. Researchers say millions could benefit from immunotherapy treatments already on the market.

sources.label: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: India experienced one of the world's most severe COVID waves, with seroprevalence above 90 per cent by mid-2022. South Asians in the US, UK, and Canada report higher rates of post-COVID fatigue and cognitive complaints than the general population. The autoantibody finding offers a testable biomarker and a path to targeted treatment for millions.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Just 10 Minutes of AI Use Can Measurably Weaken Your Problem-Solving Skills. A New Study Says the Damage May Compound Over Time.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Participants who asked ChatGPT for direct answers performed significantly worse when the tool was taken away. Those who used it for hints did not. The distinction matters for every knowledge worker in the diaspora.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian Americans are the most tech-forward ethnic group in the US, with disproportionate representation in engineering, data science, and product management — exactly the roles where AI tools are most deeply embedded.
